questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The vehicle has the right-of-way.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Shoulder work ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles display an orange and red triangle on the back. These include farm tractors, road maintenance vehicles, and animal-drawn carts.

questions.question: A broken yellow line down the center of a road means:

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not permitted from either direction.
Passing is permitted from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is permitted from either direction.
questions.explanation: Broken yellow lines separate traffic lanes on a two-lane road. Any driver can pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A blood alcohol concentration of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Has no effect on your driving.
Does not put other drivers at risk.
Doubles your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doubles your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol concentration nearly doubles your risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead has many curves.
There is a sharp curve in the road ahead.
The road ahead may be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead may be slippery.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light pointing right means:

options.text: Turn in that direction after slowing down and checking for traffic.
Do not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
Turn in that direction after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must wait until a green light or green arrow appears. Never turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, you should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help other drivers see you, even if they do not help you see much better.

questions.question: At a red traffic light with a green arrow, you may go in the direction of the arrow if:

options.text: You first come to a complete stop.
You wait until the light changes.
You are in the correct lane and the roadway is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the correct lane and the roadway is clear.
questions.explanation: If you are in a lane with a green arrow, you can go in that direction when the way is clear. This is true whether the arrow appears alone or with another signal.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
Expect all other drivers and pedestrians to yield to you.
Drive close to the parked vehicles to leave room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and parked vehicles. A person may step out of a parked car or from between cars without looking. A driver may start moving before seeing you.

questions.question: When should you return to your original lane after passing?

options.text: When you feel you are far enough ahead of the other vehicle.
When the other driver signals you to return.
When you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Use your right turn signal before returning to the right lane. It is safe to return when you can see the entire vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When entering traffic from a parked position at the curb, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a large gap to match the speed of traffic.
Wait for two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large gap to match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to reach the same speed as other traffic.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit on a state road when no other speed is posted?

options.text: 70 mph.
55 mph.
40 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 55 mph.
questions.explanation: The speed limit on state roads is 55 miles per hour. Follow posted speed limits if they are different.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered railroad gate. After the gate rises, wait until you can see clearly in both directions and you are sure no trains are coming before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: If you are following a school bus or tank truck, what should you do?

options.text: Pass them on the right.
Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
Drive closer behind them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: School buses and tank trucks must stop at all railroad crossings. Be ready to stop if you are following one of these vehicles and they stop at railroad tracks.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down before entering the curve.
Slow down to the freeway speed limit.
Start braking after you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You may not see hazards ahead, and braking in a curve can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: Directly behind the truck body.
On the left side of the cab.
On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck body.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck body.
questions.explanation: Trucks have large blind spots. The driver cannot see vehicles behind or to the side. If you cannot see the driver's face in their side mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: When passing another car, when do you have enough space to return to the driving lane?

options.text: When the other driver signals you to re-enter the lane.
When you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
When you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, there is a safe distance between your vehicles. Then it is safe to return to the driving lane.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Drive close behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.
Drive farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
Drive one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you drive too close behind a truck, the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Driving too close is dangerous because you need space to stop if the truck stops suddenly.

questions.question: How can you see vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Use your inside rearview mirror.
Use your outside rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots cannot be seen in your mirrors. You must look over your shoulders to check your blind spots.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space in front of your vehicle?

options.text: When following a station wagon.
When following a passenger vehicle.
When following a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Allow extra space behind motorcycles. They can stop faster than other vehicles. Motorcycles are also hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This is a yellow warning sign with black markings. It tells you that a divided highway is starting. You must keep to the right side of the road.

questions.question: What should you do if an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching you?

options.text: Pull over to the right side of the road and stop completely.
Keep driving, but try to stay out of its way.
Drive faster to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: The law requires you to move over for police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances using flashing lights and sirens. Pull over to the right edge of the road as close as you can. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: Defensive driving is:

options.text: Driving aggressively.
Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
More dangerous than not driving defensively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means using safe strategies to prevent crashes. You adjust your driving for weather, how you feel, and the actions of other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians.

questions.question: What happens to stopping distances and crash severity as vehicle speed increases?

options.text: They decrease.
They are not affected.
They increase.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase.
questions.explanation: When you drive faster, it takes longer to stop. Higher speeds also cause more severe crashes.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam headlights. If you cannot see ahead, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is always safe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Driving speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous. It frustrates drivers behind you, causing them to make risky passing moves. The safest approach is to drive with traffic flow and within the speed limit.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?

options.text: Neither lane may pass.
Both lanes may pass.
The right lane may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neither lane may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow markings separate lanes with traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: When driving near a large truck, what should you do?

options.text: Follow closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid staying beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid staying beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots on each side. Do not drive beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: How should you properly make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the center line before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach from the right lane, but move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Signal early to warn other drivers. Slow down and use the right lane, staying as close to the right curb as safely possible.

questions.question: What are "No zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and maneuver safely.
Areas where cars have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Areas where cars have several car lengths between them and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and maneuver safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots around trucks and buses where cars cannot be seen. They are also areas where cars are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or maneuver safely. Being in a "No zone" greatly increases the risk of a crash.
